messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'rwd-asia-gpu-1' available GPUs < 10% (6/64 free). Queue growth detected on serving-route /v1/generate. Paging on-call (pager duty): @lee :rotating_light:
lee: Acked. Looking now. What is the immediate customer impact?
incident-bot: 5 customers reporting 500/429 spikes; avg p95 latency for /v1/generate jumped from 220ms -> 2.4s. Queue length: 14k waiting, backlog rate 120 reqs/min.
marie: I'm seeing autoscaler logs: attempted scale +8 -> hit hard cap of 8 additional nodes (org quota). Policy didn't allow burst. autoscaler event snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] scale_recommendation: +8
[2026-03-15T03:12:06Z] scale_attempt: failed quota_limit_exceeded
[2026-03-15T03:12:06Z] reason: org_quota_max_nodes_reached
```
lee: Oof. That explains backlog. Can we temporarily increase quota or open a safety override?
sanjay: Runtime team: we also have driver noise on ~4 nodes. dmesg shows repeated Xid 13/31 and occasional kernel OOMs. Example:
```
Mar 15 03:10:41 node-gpu-47 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID: 2048, GPU context corrupted
Mar 15 03:11:07 node-gpu-47 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2050 (python) total_vm: 1234567kB
```
frank: Oncall infra: There's also a flurry of node flaps in the last 12m; autoscaler is conservative and is scaling down some nodes due to perceived instability. Might be thrashing.
sara: Customer SLOs: a few high-tier customers are hitting retries. Ops: open incident severity to P1?
lee: Setting P1. Notifying customer success. @sanjay, can you triage driver errors? Any quick mitigations?
sanjay: Short-term plan: 1) cordon the noisy nodes, drain workloads to healthy GPUs; 2) restart nvidia driver on affected nodes; 3) if driver restart fails, disable affected nodes from pool. Trying step 1 now.
frank: I'm toggling autoscaler to ignore scale-down for 10m to avoid thrash: 
`kubectl annotate hpa gpu-autoscaler rwd/ignore-scale-down=true --overwrite`
marie: I'm submitting a temporary quota increase request to infra admin (manual override) for +12 nodes and toggling burst policy. Patch posted to control plane. ETA ~8-12m for approval.
ops-bot: APPROVAL REQUEST: quota increase for org-redwood: +12 nodes submitted to infra-admins. Ticket #INC-8421.
lee: Good. Also, can we route low-priority batch workloads to CPU pool to free GPUs?
sanjay: Implemented routing override: low-priority label -> cpu-pool. Command: 
```
rwctl routes update --route /batch --pool cpu-pool --priority low --apply
```
lee: That freed ~9% effective GPU capacity instantly. Queue dropped ~1.1k.
marie: Driver restart attempts on node-gpu-47 failed (module unload error). Logs: `nvidia: failed to remove module - device busy`. Trying graceful node reboot now (cordon + drain done).
sanjay: Rebooting node-gpu-47. Watching.
frank: Reboot completed, driver module loaded cleanly on node-gpu-47. No Xid repeat yet.
sanjay: Rolling restart across 3 most-noisy hosts (47, 52, 59) with stagger 90s between reboots to avoid simultaneous capacity loss.
lee: Also enabling degrade-route for high-latency flows to return 503 fast for known non-critical customers to cut downstream retries.
sara: CS alerted: "Some customers may see transient errors; we are mitigating. Engineering is working on restore."
incident-bot: update: queue length 9.2k -> 5.5k after routing + reboots; p95 latency 2.4s -> 800ms.
marie: Autoscaler manual override approved. Increasing pool max_nodes by +12 and enabling burst mode. Done.
frank: New nodes provisioning; 6 came up healthy, 2 failed with driver init errors (same Xid pattern). Marking those unhealthy and requeuing.
sanjay: Correlation: noisy nodes share a specific driver build 525.85.0. Non-noisy ones are 525.81.0. Repro steps and logs attached to ticket.
lee: Action: pin runtime to known-good driver 525.81.0 and block rollout of 525.85.0 until we root cause. @sanjay please create rollback playbook.
sanjay: Creating rollback doc now. Patch to fleet rollouts: `fleetctl set-driver-version 525.81.0 --scope rwd-asia-gpu-1 --force` (will drain+reprovision).
marie: Noted for postmortem: quota headroom was insufficient and burst policy default prevented immediate scale. Need safer defaults and faster manual override runbook.
lee: Current customer impact: majority of traffic restored; impacted list: cust-17 (SLA risk), cust-42 (retrying), cust-8 (degraded). CS is prioritizing proactive outreach to cust-17.
sara: Created CS status update draft and pushed to #customer-notifications.
ops-bot: Pager rotation: @lee -> @marie in 20m for handoff.
lee: Handoff to Marie in 20. I'll remain available for the next 40m.
marie: Taking lead. Next steps: 1) finalize driver rollback on remaining noisy nodes; 2) audit autoscaler policy and add a temporary farm-level emergency quota flag; 3) schedule postmortem and RCA.
sanjay: RCA root cause hypothesis: new driver binary (525.85.0) triggers memory leak under certain kernel combos, causing OOM and Xid wave; autoscaler response and quota constraints amplified customer impact.
lee: Evidence collection: save dmesg, nvidia-smi -q, kernel logs, and core dumps to /incidents/4210091111/artifacts.
frank: I pushed artifacts and a minimal timeline to the ticket.
sara: Customers updated. No escalations to legal yet.
incident-bot: STATUS CHANGE: mitigations in place; partial service restored. Incident severity: P1 -> P2 pending full recovery.
lee: Will follow up with postmortem owner assignment. Closing initial paging loop.
marie: Assigning postmortem owner: @sanjay. Please have draft within 48h.
sanjay: Will do. Adding action items: autoscaler policy change, driver rollout gating, emergency quota runbook, and improved routing for batch workloads.
lee: Thanks team. Leaving thread but oncall remains reachable. :handshake:
